question: A developer wants to build an agent that autonomously reads files, runs shell commands, and edits code, without writing the loop that submits tool results back to the model and checks the stop reason on every turn. Which approach removes that burden, and why?
options: A) Use the Client SDK's messages API directly, since it already executes tools on your behalf whenever the stop reason is tool_use.
B) Use the Agent SDK, since it runs the same agent loop and built-in tool execution that powers Claude Code, so tool calls are handled without custom loop code.
C) Use an evaluator-optimizer workflow, since a second LLM call automatically executes tools for the first LLM call in that pattern.
D) Use a prompt-chaining workflow, since chaining removes the need for any tool execution because each step only reads the prior step's text output.
correct_answers: B) Use the Agent SDK, since it runs the same agent loop and built-in tool execution that powers Claude Code, so tool calls are handled without custom loop code.
explanations: Incorrect -- with the Client SDK, the developer must implement the tool loop themselves, calling their own tool executor and resubmitting results each time the stop reason is tool_use.
Correct -- the Agent SDK gives Claude built-in tool execution and the same agent loop and context management that power Claude Code, so the developer doesn't implement the tool loop manually.
Incorrect -- evaluator-optimizer describes a generate-and-critique relationship between two LLM calls; it doesn't provide built-in tool execution.
Incorrect -- prompt chaining is a sequence of LLM calls passing text between steps; it doesn't inherently involve or eliminate tool execution.
